data.description:
## Context / Problem
The deployed MCP server mints op-cert signatures it can never verify. Every attestation it
produces — including the completion-verifier attestation it signs on every close — is
permanently uncertifiable on the same box.

Observed 2026-08-27 against the LIVE MCP server
(`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`, container `compose-mcp-1`), signing and then
immediately verifying on the same server:

```
sign_manifest {"ticket_id": "ruby-griffinish-goitered", "manifest": ["probe: ..."]}
  -> {"algorithm": "sshsig", "key_id": "9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65",
      "signed_at": 1787815608646086582, "envelope": "{...}"}          # SUCCEEDS

verify_signature {"ticket_id": "ruby-griffinish-goitered"}
  -> {"verified": false, "verdict": "foreign_key", "step_count": 1,
      "key_id": "9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65", "head_sha": "unknown",
      "reason": "this environment has no op-cert public key; it cannot certify any signature"}
```

The signature is not foreign — the principal matches this environment. It is unverifiable
because the matching PUBLIC key is absent.

## Mechanism
`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:528-535`

```python
own_pub = _opcert_own_public_key(tracker)
if not own_pub:
    return {
        **base,
        "verified": False,
        "verdict": "foreign_key",
        "reason": "this environment has no op-cert public key; it cannot certify any signature",
    }
```

`_opcert_own_public_key` reads the public key from the TRACKER directory, but the deployment
supplies only the PRIVATE key, via `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`, from a mount that has no
public half. Verified in-container:

```
$ docker exec compose-mcp-1 ls -l /run/secrets/
-rw-------. 1 root root 298 Aug 26 18:24 mcp-static-tokens.json
-rw-------. 1 root root 411 Aug 26 18:24 opcert-ed25519-key          # private key only, no .pub

$ docker exec compose-mcp-1 ls -la /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets/ | grep -iE 'opcert|env-id|ensure'
-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 152 Aug 27 01:38 .ensure-applied
-rw-r--r--. 1 root root  37 Aug 27 01:09 .env-id                     # no .opcert-key.pub
```

Env: `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY=/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key`,
`REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID=9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65`.

The tracker's `.env-id` is dated 2026-08-27 01:09 and the container started 01:38 — i.e. the
tracker was re-cloned (see `7be0edb7132d fix(mcp): re-clone an unusable tickets store`). The
re-clone regenerated `.env-id` but never restored `.opcert-key.pub`. `fsck` on the same server
names exactly this failure mode:

```
ENV_ID_MISMATCH: ... This is the signature of a tracker re-clone that did not carry over its
git-ignored local state (.env-id, .opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub, .ensure-applied).
```

so the diagnostic already exists; nothing acts on it, and signing proceeds regardless.

## Impact
rebar mints exactly two op-cert kinds (ADR 0049): plan-review at claim and
completion-verifier at close. On this server both are signed-but-uncertifiable. Concretely,
closing probe bug `weary-paralyzing-xanclomys` returned
`"completion_signature": {"signed": true, "cause": "signed"}` — a certificate that
`verify_signature` cannot certify. Any project that later enables
`verify.require_environment` + `verify.opcert_enforce_since` (the enforcement flip in
`infra/runbooks/mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md`) would find every attestation this server
produced rejected as `foreign_key`, and the audit trail silently records certificates that
prove nothing today.

Signing SUCCEEDS while verification is structurally impossible, so nothing surfaces the
problem at the moment the certificate is minted.

## Reproduction
1. Against the deployed MCP server, call `sign_manifest` on any ticket with a one-item manifest.
2. Observe it succeeds and returns an `sshsig` envelope.
3. Call `verify_signature` on the same ticket.
4. Observe `verdict: "foreign_key"`, `verified: false`, reason "this environment has no op-cert public key".

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: On the deployed MCP server, a `sign_manifest` immediately followed by `verify_signature` on the same ticket returns `verdict: "certified"`, `verified: true`.
- [ ] AC2: The deployment materializes the public key half wherever `_opcert_own_public_key` reads it, derived from or shipped alongside `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`.
- [ ] AC3: A completion attestation signed by a close through the deployed server verifies as `certified` via `verify_signature` with `kind="completion-verifier"`.
- [ ] AC4: Signing refuses, or emits an explicit warning, when the environment cannot verify its own signatures — a certificate that can never be certified must not be minted silently.
- [ ] AC5: The tracker re-clone path restores or regenerates the git-ignored local state it destroys (`.opcert-key`, `.opcert-key.pub`, `.env-id`), or fails loudly instead of leaving the environment unable to certify.
- [ ] AC6: A startup or deploy health check fails when the signing key has no usable public counterpart, so this cannot regress silently.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] DD1: AC1 and AC3 demonstrated against a deployed MCP server.
- [ ] DD2: AC4 and AC5 covered by regression tests.
- [ ] DD3: AC6 check runs in the deploy path.
data.title: Deployed MCP server signs op-certs it cannot verify: the signing key has no public counterpart, so every attestation is foreign_key
